tier_reason: Upgraded from B to A on stronger evidence. The peer-reviewed paper (Lemire & Kaser, J. Cryptographic Engineering 6(3), DOI 10.1007/s13389-015-0110-5, arXiv 1503.03465) states GCC 4.8 -O2 and an Intel i7-4770 at 3.4 GHz, and its public artifact repo (lemire/StronglyUniversalStringHashing, benchmark/benchmark.cc and benchmark/variablelengthbenchmark.cc with the include/City/City.c port) benchmarks CLHASH against CityHash64WithSeed: 0.16 vs 0.23 cycles/byte at 4 kB. The xxh3 margin in the record comes only from the rurban SMHasher table, where the row numbers match exactly (22932.36 vs 20853.74 MiB/s); that part stays B-tier, since the compiler version is not stated there.

corrections.baseline: CityHash (CityHash64WithSeed, the paper's C port of v1.1.1); secondarily xxHash (xxh3) via SMHasher
corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper Table 5 (i7-4770): 0.16 vs 0.23 cycles/byte for CityHash on 4 kB inputs (authors: 'almost 45% faster'; about 40% faster on inputs over 64 B, similar speed at 32 B or less) and 0.45 vs 0.48 cycles/byte at 64 B. Separately, the rurban SMHasher bulk test (262144-byte keys, Ryzen 5 3350G) gives 22932.36 vs 20853.74 MiB/s for xxh3, about 10% faster (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Paper: GNU GCC 4.8 with -O2 (benchmark code in lemire/StronglyUniversalStringHashing). SMHasher: CMake Release build with -march=native -std=c++11 per rurban/smhasher CMakeLists.txt; compiler version not stated.
corrections.hardware: Paper: Intel i7-4770 (Haswell) at 3.4 GHz, 32 GB DDR3-1600, Turbo Boost and hyper-threading disabled. SMHasher: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (default table).
corrections.workload: Paper: hashing random inputs from 8 B to 8 kB (Table 5 reports 64 B and 4 kB), timed with rdtsc over 40 million input words per length, random-bit generation excluded. SMHasher: bulk speed test with 262144-byte keys, run with many hash functions on the same machine and build in rurban/smhasher.
corrections.caveats: The paper-era CLHASH code (StronglyUniversalStringHashing, 2015) is not the current simdhash/clhash library, and the CityHash baseline was the authors' own C port of CityHash 1.1.1 rather than upstream C++. Against xxh3, CLHash wins only on bulk data (about 10% in SMHasher) and is about 2.3x slower on small keys (67.22 vs 29.46 cycles/hash). SMHasher flags a PerlinNoise quality issue, and the paper reports CLHASH fails the SMHasher avalanche test. It is x64 (PCLMULQDQ+SSE4.2) or ARM PMULL only. The README's own claim is '20 to 40x faster' than a naive Java-like polynomial hash, plus about 0.1 cycles/byte on Skylake. The repo was transferred from lemire/clhash (which redirects) to the simdhash org.

notes: SMHasher row numbers and all metadata check out (Apache-2.0, not fork/archived, 302 stars, last commit 2026-05-23). The tier was upgraded to A because the peer-reviewed paper plus its artifact repo meet every A criterion against CityHash; the xxh3 comparison is B-tier only. The orchestrator may want to present CityHash as the primary baseline.

tier_reason: The rurban SMHasher README table (a well-known independent suite, public code, CPU named Ryzen 5 3350G) has falkhash at 52401.48 MiB/s against xxh3 20853.74, wyhash 22640.53 and City128 14472.20, all matching the record and doc/falkhash.txt. It is not A because the table states no compiler version. The author's README has only raw cycles/byte and SMHasher output, with no baseline comparison (that alone would be C).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rurban/smhasher links a prebuilt falkhash.asm object (falkhash-elf64.o / falkhash-macho64.o), so the CMake Release -march=native flags do not apply to the hash itself; the compiler version is not stated. The author's README separately reports 0.074-0.25 cycles/byte with GCC 4.9.2, clang 3.5.0, MSVC 19.00.23026 and MSVC 18.00.31101, with no baseline comparison.
corrections.caveats: The SMHasher numbers are for the v1 hand-written assembly (falkhash.asm). The repo now ships the v2 C-intrinsics implementation, whose hash values differ and which the independent table does not benchmark. SMHasher now rates falkhash POOR (Sparse and LongNeighbors failures), contradicting the README's 'passes all of smhasher's tests', and the author calls it an 'Exotic Probably Shitty Hash'. The win is bulk-only: on small keys it is about 4x slower than xxh3 (122.70 vs 29.46 cycles/hash). It needs x64 AES-NI. The author's README has only raw cycles/byte and SMHasher output on decade-old CPUs, with no direct baseline numbers. It has low notability (48 stars) and has been unmaintained since 2015. Unlicense: no patent grant.

notes: Numbers and metadata verified (Unlicense, 48 stars, last commit 2015-11-13, not fork/archived). The main issues for enrichment are that the benchmarked code is the old asm v1, not the repo's current C code, and SMHasher's POOR quality rating.

tier_reason: The rurban SMHasher README table (a well-known independent suite, public code, Ryzen 5 3350G) lists FarmHash32 at 22136.14 MiB/s against xxh3 20853.74 and City32 5745.83, matching the record and doc/FarmHash32.txt. It is not A because no compiler version is stated. FarmHash's own README gives no speed numbers.

corrections.caveats: Only FarmHash32 (32-bit output, SSE4/AVX path) wins. FarmHash64 (12929.54 MiB/s) is slower than both xxh3 (20853.74) and City64 (14390.09) on bulk, and FarmHash128 (14454.12) is slower than xxh128 (19259.99). Even FarmHash32 is slower than xxh3 on small keys (46.75 vs 29.46 cycles/hash), and the xxh3 comparison is 32-bit vs 64-bit output. FarmHash's own README/NEWS make no quantified speed claim, so the win comes from the independent SMHasher table, where rurban lists FarmHash among the fastest x86_64 hashes without quality problems but notes 'not portable, too machine specific'. The 2026-06-05 last commit only merges old PRs (a README rename and a small fix); substantive development stopped in 2019.
